_meta.indication: Treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 5 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study MP-104-NM-001 (Study 1 in the Emflaza label)
pivotal_trials.phase: Not explicitly stated; adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week study conducted in the US and Canada; patients randomized to deflazacort (0.9 or 1.2 mg/kg/day), an active comparator, or placebo, with placebo comparison at 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: 196 male pediatric patients 5 to 15 years of age with documented mutation of the dystrophin gene and DMD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from Baseline to Week 12 in average muscle strength score of 18 muscle groups (modified MRC 11-point scale)
pivotal_trials.n: 196 randomized; 51 deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day and 50 placebo compared at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: Change from baseline at Week 12 in average muscle strength score: deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day LS Mean 0.15 (95% CI 0.01, 0.28) vs placebo -0.10 (95% CI -0.23, 0.03); P-value 0.017

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) are Cushingoid appearance, weight increased, increased appetite, upper respiratory tract infection, cough, pollakiuria, hirsutism, central obesity, and nasopharyngitis. In Study 1 at 12 weeks vs placebo: Cushingoid appearance 33% vs 12%, weight increased 20% vs 6%, increased appetite 14% vs 2%.
target_moa: Deflazacort is a glucocorticoid (inactive ester pro-drug metabolized to active 21-desacetyldeflazacort) that acts as an anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive agent, binding glucocorticoid receptors to up-regulate anti-inflammatory proteins; it may decrease inflammation and fibrosis in muscles affected by DMD

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the review section states Not applicable.

description.text: Expanded use for Duchenne muscular dystrophy to include patients 2 years of age and older

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for an expansion of the use of Emflaza (deflazacort) for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, to include patients 2 years of age and older.

summary.text: Deflazacort received Orphan Drug designation (Aug 16, 2013) and Fast Track designation (Nov 21, 2014) for DMD, and Rare Pediatric Disease designation (Aug 10, 2015). The NDA was granted priority review and approved via a standard (full, not accelerated) approval, effective on the date of the approval letter.

citations.quote: The Agency granted Orphan Drug designation to deflazacort for the treatment of DMD on August 16, 2013, and Fast Track designation on November 21, 2014. Marathon requested Rare Pediatric Disease designation on March 20, 2015, which was granted on August 10, 2015.
Deflazacort was granted a priority review designation for this application.
We have completed our review of these applications, as amended. They are approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.
